items.title: Top bar visual pass: Tabler icons, borderless icon buttons, quieter pane toggles
items.summary: A visual pass on the top bar and icons. Every icon now comes from Tabler Icons (outline), drawn a little larger (16px) with a slightly heavier line. The top-bar icon buttons (Home, Refresh, Debug, Copy guide, ?, Re-do, Collapse threads, Documents, Settings, the update icon) lose their boxes and match the card action buttons; the PR link chip keeps its box. A pressed segment in a toggle (Guide/Source, unified/split) now shows a light tint with bold text instead of solid black, so Submit review is the only solid dark button in the bar.

items.title: Guide prompts: encourage ::: background blocks where they fit
items.summary: The guide now writes a Background block where it fits, instead of almost never. A Background block is how the existing system works, on a quiet tint that a reader who knows the codebase can skip. The problem card usually carries one, and any later card that leans on existing-system knowledge a newcomer lacks may carry one. Still at most one per card, and never about the change itself.

items.caveats: Only guides written after installing this build show it; existing guides keep their text until you Re-do them.

items.title: Teach replaces Guide as the guide's prompts; drop the 'How it's built up' card
items.summary: The guide now writes in the Teach style, and Teach is no longer a separate persona. Its instructions replace the old guide's outright: it teaches the change step by step, in full sentences, spelling out cause and effect and explaining terms where they first appear. The "How it's built up" card is gone. Settings → Personas now lists Guide, Second opinion and Clarity, and Re-do is a plain button again unless you add a persona that can write a whole guide.

items.caveats: Existing installs keep a stale "Teach" persona in their saved settings. Delete it in Settings → Personas, or reset the data. Reviews written before this build keep their old guide, including any "How it's built up" card.

items.title: Fresh install: Small model shows 'saved model claude-haiku-5-5 is no longer offered' (static default saved / live default not applied)
items.summary: Settings → Models: the Small model no longer shows "Saved model … is no longer offered" for a model you never picked. On a fresh install or after a data reset, Small uses the built-in default, and that default was being treated as a saved choice. The error now appears only when a model you actually saved is no longer listed.

items.title: Settings → Version: 'Show previews' shows ticked while the saved setting is off (no previews listed)
items.summary: Settings → Version: the Show previews box always shows the saved setting. Before, if the service changed under an open Settings page (a channel switch that reset the data, a restart, or a change from the CLI or another tab), the box could stay ticked while previews were hidden. Now every status read and Refresh puts the box back in line with the saved value, and Refresh reloads the status before the channels.

items.title: Teach: scannable structure (sub-headings, bullets) + tinted background blocks
items.summary: Teach cards are easier to scan: short paragraphs, sub-headings and bullets. Now and then a card opens with a Background block, which sits in place on a quiet grey tint with a muted BACKGROUND tag and its own citation chips. The change is only in Teach's prompts; the Guide and other personas are unchanged.

items.title: Settings: choose the default Guide persona (used for new reviews and Re-do guide)
items.summary: Settings → Personas has a Default guide picker. The persona you pick there (any enabled persona that can write a guide) writes the guide for new reviews and for a plain Re-do; Re-do with still lets you choose a persona for one run. Each review records which persona wrote it. If the default persona is deleted, disabled or can no longer write a guide, the Guide stands in and Settings says so in one line.

items.title: 'Help me understand' drops most of the rewrite and leaves citations on the wrong paragraphs (paragraph-slot merge)
items.summary: Help me understand now shows the whole rewrite. Before, a press could keep only the card's original paragraph slots, dropping the new lists, steps and example and leaving citation chips on the wrong paragraphs. Now the rewrite replaces the card body in full, each paragraph with its own citations, while diagrams and follow-up suggestions are kept and Undo restores the previous text. The same applies to persona tabs, thread replies and the ? mode's Rewrite cards.

items.title: Extension panel: a slow or interrupted ask is resent to the same service under its other host name and stored twice
items.summary: The browser extension no longer resends a side-panel question or an "open review" request after it fails or times out. It used to retry under the service's other local address, which could store the same question twice. A failed ask now shows "request failed" instead.

items.title: Guide personas that own their prompts (whole-file forks) + Re-do with…
items.summary: Guide personas can now own their own prompts. A persona whose folder `prompts/personas/<id>/` contains `reader.md` can write a whole guide; any template in that folder replaces the shared one of the same name (whole file), and the rest fall back to the shared prompts. Each review records which Guide persona wrote it, and every main-agent task on it uses that persona's templates, model and style; card personas run on top of it. The Re-do menu gains "Re-do with <persona>" for each such persona (it replaces the review, like Re-do). `mise run persona:fork -- <id> <file.md…>` copies base prompts into a fork, and Settings warns when a forked file's base has changed since. An installed build can be pointed at an edited prompts folder with UNVIBE_PROMPTS_DIR.

items.caveats: Data reset needed: the stored review shape changed (data format 9). On first start Unvibe shows a reset notice; resetting moves your old data aside (nothing is deleted). Export unposted Outbox drafts first, then set your models, Guide and personas again afterwards.

items.title: Extension: 'Review in Unvibe' button lands in GitHub dialogs (e.g. Finish your review); anchor only in the PR header
items.summary: The browser extension's "Review in Unvibe" button now appears only in a pull request page's header. It no longer lands inside GitHub dialogs such as "Finish your review", popovers or overlays, and it no longer shows on pages GitHub serves under a PR address that aren't the PR itself, such as the single sign-on screen. There is exactly one button per page.

items.title: Experimental: '?' mode, pick terms across the guide, then bulk-rewrite cards to explain them
items.summary: Experimental "?" mode: a new ? button in the review's top bar (next to Refresh, Debug and Copy guide) turns on term picking. Select any words you don't understand in the guide cards; each is highlighted and added to a tray at the bottom of the guide, where you can remove terms or press Rewrite cards. Every guide card is then rewritten in place, more slowly, for a reader who doesn't know those terms: each card's rewrite sees the whole guide, so terms are introduced once and used consistently. It is one Help me understand press per card, so each card's Undo steps back on its own. Titles, order, anchors and threads stay as they are. Hidden in the static demo.

items.title: Replace simpler/deeper with one repeatable 'Help me understand' (explain more slowly)
items.summary: The − ●● + depth stepper on cards is replaced by one icon button, "Help me understand". Each press rewrites the card more slowly than its current text: the skipped steps filled in, terms defined where they first appear, a concrete walk-through with real values, smaller leaps, and the why where only the what was given. It never gets shorter by dropping content, keeps every citation on its paragraph, and keeps the structure, examples and diagrams. Press again to slow it down further; Undo steps back one press at a time. It works the same on thread replies and persona tabs, and Copy as Markdown copies what is shown. The simple / standard / deep levels and the "deeper" direction are gone; use Ask to say what is confusing.

items.title: Start page author search misses the author's open PRs that don't request your review
items.summary: "Waiting on your review" now also lists open PRs you have already reviewed (GitHub drops the request once you review), in "Requested of you" unless a request still puts them in your team group. Typing or picking an author searches GitHub for all their open PRs: requested of you, of your team, and a "Not requested of you" group for the rest. Drafts and approved PRs are never filtered out, and "No open PRs by …" appears only when the author has none.

items.title: Go-deeper card content: generate on demand only by default (autoGoDeeper off)

items.title: Copy the whole guide as Markdown (prose cards only, no code or comments)
items.summary: A new copy icon in the review's top bar, next to Refresh and Debug ("Copy guide as Markdown"), copies the whole guide: the review title, then each card's heading and text at the depth it's shown, always the Guide version. Citations follow each paragraph as GitHub links (plain path:lines for local reviews), inline code is kept, and each diagram becomes a short placeholder. Code blocks, threads, findings, plotlines and "Updated since…" sections are left out.
